Write an Object or a Text Into a Log File

Source: R/report.R
report.Rd

Writes a character string or a data object into a text file, after its previous content if required. Convenient to build log files.

Usage

report(
  data,
  output = "log.txt",
  path,
  append = FALSE,
  rownames_kept = FALSE,
  vector_cat = FALSE,
  noquote = TRUE,
  sep = 2,
  safer_check = TRUE,
  lib_path = NULL,
  error_text = ""
)

Arguments

data

Object to write (single value, vector, factor, matrix, table, data frame, list, ...). If NULL, nothing is done, with no warning.

output

Single character string: name of the output file.

path

Single character string: path of the existing folder of the output file. No default value.

append

Single logical value. If TRUE, data is written after the content of the output file (created if it does not exist). If FALSE (default), the output file must not exist: an existing file is never overwritten (error).

rownames_kept

Single logical value. Keep the row names of matrices, tables and data frames? Warning: the names above the values of 1D tables are row names, removed if FALSE.

vector_cat

Single logical value. If TRUE, vectors of length > 1 are written with cat() (values separated by a space, names not written), otherwise as printed in the console. Vectors of length 1 are always written with cat(). Here, vectors are atomic vectors with no attribute other than names: factors, dates and lists are always written as printed in the console.

noquote

Single logical value. If TRUE, character vectors (of length > 1, with vector_cat = FALSE), character matrices and character arrays are written without quotes. No effect on the other objects.

sep

Single positive integer: number of empty lines written after data.

safer_check

Single logical value. If TRUE (default), checks before running that the required packages and functions are installed and that the classical R operators (like <-) are not masked by another package or by a user-defined object of the global environment. These checks take time at each call: set FALSE in loops and inside other safer-r functions, to avoid repeating them.

lib_path

Vector of character strings: paths of existing extra library folders containing the required packages (e.g., packages installed without admin rights). They are searched after the current .libPaths() during the call (the current libraries keep priority), and .libPaths() is restored on exit. If NULL (default), only the current .libPaths() are used.

error_text

Single character string added to the error messages (e.g., " INSIDE pkg1::fun1()") to name the calling functions. NULL is converted into "".

Value

No return value (invisible NULL), called for its side effect: data is written into the output file of the path folder.

See also

capture.output, cat.

Author

Gael Millot

Haiding Wang

Yushi Han

Examples

# See also https://safer-r.github.io/saferDev/articles/report.html
# Write in the results.txt file of a new temporary folder:
tempo_dir <- base::tempfile(pattern = "dir", tmpdir = base::tempdir(check = FALSE), fileext = "")
base::dir.create(path = tempo_dir, showWarnings = TRUE, recursive = FALSE, mode = "0777")
saferDev::report(data = "THE FOLLOWING VECTOR IS:", output = "results.txt", path = tempo_dir,
    append = TRUE, rownames_kept = FALSE, vector_cat = FALSE, noquote = TRUE, sep = 1,
    safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
saferDev::report(data = 1:3, output = "results.txt", path = tempo_dir, append = TRUE,
    rownames_kept = FALSE, vector_cat = FALSE, noquote = FALSE, sep = 2, safer_check = TRUE,
    lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
saferDev::report(data = "THE FOLLOWING DATA FRAME IS:", output = "results.txt",
    path = tempo_dir, append = TRUE, rownames_kept = FALSE, vector_cat = FALSE, noquote = TRUE,
    sep = 1, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL, error_text = "")
saferDev::report(data = base::data.frame(A = 1:3, B = base::letters[1:3], row.names = NULL,
    check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE, fix.empty.names = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    output = "results.txt", path = tempo_dir, append = TRUE, rownames_kept = FALSE,
    vector_cat = FALSE, noquote = FALSE, sep = 1, safer_check = TRUE, lib_path = NULL,
    error_text = "")
base::cat(base::readLines(con = base::file.path(tempo_dir, "results.txt", fsep = "/"), n = -1L,
    ok = TRUE, warn = TRUE, encoding = "unknown", skipNul = FALSE), file = "", sep = "\n",
    fill = FALSE, labels = NULL, append = FALSE)
#> THE FOLLOWING VECTOR IS:
#> 
#> [1] 1 2 3
#> 
#> 
#> THE FOLLOWING DATA FRAME IS:
#> 
#>  A B
#>  1 a
#>  2 b
#>  3 c
#> 
base::unlink(x = tempo_dir, recursive = TRUE, force = FALSE, expand = TRUE) # folder removed
